lesson.title: Representing and Grouping Data
lesson.summary: Choose a clear way to present discrete data, group values sensibly when there are many of them, and read the information a display is designed to show.

objectives.text: Represent discrete data in tables, diagrams and charts, including pie charts, bar charts and line graphs.
Group discrete data and represent grouped data graphically.

sections.heading: Choosing a useful data display
sections.body: A table keeps exact values organised. A bar chart is useful for comparing separate categories, such as different types of journey. A pie chart shows how a whole is divided into parts. A line graph can show values changing over time. Choose the display that makes the comparison or pattern easiest for the reader to see.

sections.heading: Grouping values fairly
sections.body: When a list contains many different numerical values, grouping can make it easier to read. Create intervals that do not overlap and cover every value, such as 0 to 4, 5 to 9 and 10 to 14. State the group boundaries clearly. Grouping summarises the data, so it may hide individual values that a full table would show.

sections.heading: Reading data with care
sections.body: Before drawing a conclusion from a chart, check its title, labels, scale and time period. A bar height or a line position only has meaning when you read the axis labels. Compare like with like, and avoid claiming a pattern that the data does not show. A clear display supports explanation, but it does not replace sensible interpretation.

practice.prompt: A community centre wants to compare the numbers attending yoga, swimming, football and art classes in one week. Which display is most suitable?
practice.explanation: A bar chart makes it easy to compare totals for separate categories such as different classes.

practice.prompt: The values 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11 and 13 are to be grouped. Which set of intervals is clear and has no overlap?
practice.explanation: The intervals 0–4, 5–9 and 10–14 cover every value once without sharing a boundary value.

practice.prompt: A table shows visitors to a museum each month from January to June. Which display is most useful for showing how the number changes over those months?
options: A pie chart with no labels
practice.explanation: A line graph is useful for showing a value changing across an ordered time period.
